notes: Open with the decision, not the market story: approve the work now and constrain spend to a 100-day proof sprint. Point to the three assumptions that must be tested before scale. Expect a question on commitment level; answer that this approves entry work and launch proof, not full national rollout.
title: The right decision now is to approve partner-led Indonesia entry work and fund a 100-day sprint that proves the few assumptions that matter most

sections.heading: Approve a bounded entry decision
sections.body: The decision required now is narrower than full market rollout: authorize partner selection, product registration, channel setup, and launch testing for Indonesia’s premium personal-care market. This matches the highest-conviction route already identified — a distributor-led, digital-first model — while keeping capital tied to evidence from the first selling cycle, not to fixed infrastructure.

sections.heading: Back the launch path with fastest learning
sections.body: A **100-day** sprint is the shortest practical window to move from strategy to real demand evidence: shortlist and sign the local partner, lock hero SKUs, prepare claims and compliance, activate marketplaces, and read early conversion, repeat, and channel economics. The objective is speed with control — enough live-market proof to confirm fit before expanding assortment, geography, or offline reach.

sections.heading: Test the three assumptions that drive scale
sections.body: Management should treat the sprint as an explicit test of only three scale assumptions. First, urban affluent consumers convert on the proposed proposition of halal trust, efficacy, and premium positioning. Second, hero SKUs in skin care, hair care, and body care win repeat without excessive discounting. Third, the partner can execute registration, marketplace operations, and fulfilment at the service level the brand needs.

sections.heading: Set clear gates before releasing more capital
sections.body: The output of the sprint is a scale/no-scale decision, not a progress report. Release the next tranche only if the partner performs, claims land with target consumers, and the initial SKU set shows clean demand signals through digital channels. If any assumption breaks, management still preserves option value: refine the proposition, replace the partner, or stop before national distribution complexity adds cost.
